links.note: Factors behind the kingdom-to-empire transition; the model answer is resources, surplus agriculture, trade and taxation carrying military strength, which is 30673's claim that military power rests on economic power. 30670 is only the definition of an empire.

Alexander's world significance, answered through his conquests and the Greek-Indian contact that followed; 30680 is the concept that introduces that contact and explains it by the Mediterranean route.
Brahmi project: Brahmi enters this chapter as the script of Ashoka's edicts, and 30689 is the edict concept. The set has no separate writing-system concept.
Planning a 3rd-century BCE journey along the Dakshinapatha with caravans is the trade-route concept 30674, not 30675 which is about trade raising producer income and tax.
'Samraj'/'rajadhiraja' as king of kings is the vocabulary of what makes an empire more than a kingdom - 30670.
Why kings expanded: access to resources and strength, i.e. the economic underpinning in 30673. 30672 is the cost of armies, the opposite direction.

Dates Panini to the Nanda reign. The set has no Nanda or grammarian concept; 30676 is the concept that puts named thinkers on the Magadhan political timeline (Buddha and Mahavira under Ajatashatru), which is the same move this item asks for.
Alexander's motive for marching east - the invasion that brought the Greek encounter, 30680. 30681-83 are the gymnosophist episode specifically.

The costly retreat from India, part of the same Greek-contact episode, 30680. Considered 30672 (campaigning at a distance is harder than it looks) but that concept's content is the economics of maintaining an army, not Alexander's return.
Keyed answer is Panini-Ashtadhyayi, so it belongs with the other Panini item on 30676; the Kautilya and Megasthenes options are distractors here, not what is being tested.
Megasthenes and the Indika: he is in this chapter as the Greek emissary at the Mauryan court, which is 30693.

Sohagaura granary inscription read as evidence of Mauryan food-security administration - part of 30691's assessment of what the Mauryas did for the people of the empire, rather than 30689 which is about what an edict is.
Sarnath lion capital taken up as the national emblem: the pillars and their symbols, 30692.
'Mitra' is one of the seven limbs in Kautilya's saptanga - 30685.
Keyed on stupas as hemispherical relic structures - Mauryan architecture read for what it was for, 30692.
'Posterity' is the chapter's word in asking why a ruler records his own deeds, which is 30690's question about Kalinga. Not 30689, the definition of an edict.
Arthashastra's laws against corruption: the Kautilyan theory of the state, 30685, which is the only concept in the set carrying the Arthashastra's content.
Guilds sharing resources and market information sit with 30675, where producers' interests and the volume of trade are the subject; 30674 is the routes themselves.
Drawbridge in Pataliputra's fortification - part of the chapter's account of the Mauryan capital and what the dynasty built, 30691. 30692 is reserved for pillars, stupas and their symbols.
Takshashila placed in the northwest: 30679 is the concept that turns to that region while Magadha rose.
Four lions back to back on the Sarnath capital - 30692's symbols.
Far-off territories breaking away under weak successors is the failure of 30671's problem - holding varied, distant populations together by administration.

Statement item in the Alexander block (the visible statement, a permanent Greek capital in Magadha, is the false one), so 30680. DEFECT: statements 1-3 are missing from the stored stem, only the third survives.
Satyameva Jayate is inscribed below the emblem taken from the Sarnath capital, so it belongs to 30692 with the other emblem items.
'Amatya' = councillors and ministers, named in 30685's description of the saptanga.
Spices as a long-distance export: goods and the volume of trade, 30675, rather than the routes themselves (30674).
Sanchi's Great Stupa as the Mauryan architectural site - 30692.
Pradakshina is explained in the chapter's treatment of stupa architecture and its use, which is 30692.
What the Arthashastra and Megasthenes imply about the state - a centralised administration, which is 30671's point that the chapter's question is administration rather than conquest.

Statement item about Kautilya's work (the visible statement, that it puts the king's welfare above his subjects', is the false one), so the Arthashastra concept 30685. DEFECT: the statement list is truncated to its last line.
Definition of an empire as many kingdoms under one ruler - 30670.
'Tributary' is part of the same definitional vocabulary that separates an empire from a kingdom, 30670; 30671 is how such an empire was actually administered.
Sanskrit words for emperor, the same item as the samraj MCQ - 30670.
'Posterity' recall, paired with its MCQ twin on 30690 (why a king records his deeds for those who come after).
Magadha as the mahajanapada that became the base of the first empires - 30677, the concept about Magadha's setting and advantages.
Ajatashatru is named in 30676 itself as the Magadhan king of the Buddha's and Mahavira's time.
Mahapadma Nanda founding the Nanda dynasty: the pre-Mauryan Magadhan timeline, which only 30676 holds. 30684 is the founding of the Mauryas.
Ashtadhyayi recall, same concept as the other two Panini items - 30676.
Porus opposing Alexander in Punjab: the northwest encounter with the Greeks, 30680.
'Gymnosophists' is the Greek name defined in 30681.
Title of Kautilya's work on governance - the Arthashastra concept 30685.
Indika and its author, the Greek emissary - 30693.
Advantages of guild membership, the short-answer twin of the guild MCQ - 30675.
Fertile Ganga plains, iron ore, forests and elephants: 30677's list of Magadha's geographical advantages.
Iron ploughs raising yields and iron weapons strengthening the army is 30678's double effect, stated in the same two halves.
Description of Alexander's northwest campaign - the Greek contact episode, 30680. 30679 is about the small northwest kingdoms before he arrived.
Subject matter of the Arthashastra - 30685, the Kautilyan account of what a state is and how it is run.
Saptanga explained limb by limb - 30685 exactly.
Kautilya's people-first view of kingship, which is 30669's opening claim that there is no country without people and an empire is defined by the people it holds.
Pataliputra's palaces, streets and crafts belong to 30691's assessment of Mauryan life; 30692 is the pillars and stupas read as symbols.
Sohagaura plate and famine granaries, the short-answer twin of the earlier MCQ - 30691.
Everyday clothing in the Mauryan period is material life under the empire, 30691.
What the polished pillars and Sarnath capital signify - 30692's reading of objects as evidence.
Why empires decline: tributary resentment, weak successors, regions breaking away - the collapse of 30671's holding-together problem.
Guilds and economic stability - 30675, where trade volume, producer income and self-organisation sit.
Political versus cultural impact of Alexander's invasion; the answer turns on the contact opened with the Hellenistic world, which is 30680.
Analysing the Arthashastra's principles as pragmatic statecraft - 30685.

Asks for the practical payoff of subjects' welfare and the answer is productivity, taxes and army support, i.e. 30673's economic underwriting of power. The plain statement of the principle itself I put on 30669.
